dedupe_keys.name: muse modular energy system simulation environment

description: MUSE, the ModUlar energy system Simulation Environment, is an open-source energy system model that simulates change in an energy system over time through agents, investors and consumers with possibly different investment strategies, who invest in production, conversion and end-use technologies across residential, power, industrial and conversion sectors. Users run the bundled default example with a single command or define their own model through a settings.toml file and input files for technologies, commodities and demands, and the package also ships further example models listed by its command-line help. It is developed at Imperial College London, which holds the copyright, and its citation file names Sara Giarola, Alexander Kell and Adam Hawkes. The framework is location independent: regions, sectors and time horizon are set in the user's input files, from one country to many regions. It is distributed as a Python package on PyPI (version 1.6.0, released 8 May 2026, Python 3.11 to 3.14) with source on GitHub and online documentation, under the GNU GPL version 3 at no cost. Caveats: results depend on the agent and technology assumptions the user supplies, and the README gives only installation and usage basics, so the full documentation is needed to build a new model. Simulation uses are long-term capacity planning and agent-based analysis of energy transitions. Related records: it compares with model-calliope and model-oemof-solph, which optimise, not simulate agent decisions.
